profile.name: NIST SP 800-41 Rev. 1 - the configuration-checkable part
profile.description:
A starting point, not an authority. Every check below cites the clause it comes from, so a reader who disagrees can argue with NIST rather than with this tool. Copy this file, delete what does not apply to your estate, and add your own - that is the point of the format.
Read `not_checkable` at the bottom before presenting a clean run: several of the publication's most important recommendations are process controls that no configuration reader can verify.

not_checkable.requirement: Formal change management process for ruleset changes
not_checkable.why: A process control. Nothing in a policy package records whether a change went through an approval workflow. Verify by evidence and interview.

not_checkable.requirement: Periodic ruleset review actually performed
not_checkable.why: This tool can show you what the ruleset looks like today and, with the Policy Diff page, what changed since a previous snapshot. It cannot show that a human reviewed it.

not_checkable.requirement: Logs and alerts are continuously monitored
not_checkable.why: Monitoring happens outside the policy package. This profile checks only that rules are configured to produce logs at all.

results.title: No rule permits Any source to Any destination on Any service
results.detail: No rule matches the forbidden condition.

source.quote: Generally, firewalls should block all inbound and outbound traffic that has not been expressly permitted by the firewall policy - traffic that is not needed by the organization. This practice, known as deny by default, decreases the risk of attack and can also reduce the volume of traffic carried on the organization's networks.

results.title: Every layer ends with an explicit, logged cleanup rule
results.detail: Every layer ends with an explicit cleanup rule.

source.note: An implicit drop enforces deny-by-default but produces no log, so denied traffic cannot be reviewed. An explicit logged cleanup rule makes the same decision visible.

results.title: Every rule is logged, so the ruleset can be reviewed against real traffic
results.detail: 1 rule(s) have no track.

source.quote: Firewall rulesets and policies should be managed by a formal change management control process because of their potential to impact security and business operations, with ruleset reviews or tests performed periodically to ensure continued compliance with the organization's policies.
source.note: The review itself is a process control this tool cannot observe. What it can check is whether the ruleset produces the evidence a review needs.
